title: Serum protein panel with machine learning separates HCC from cirrhosis
summary: A staged DIA-MS discovery, verification and PRM validation workflow in 662 individuals (373 HCC patients, 289 non-HCC) quantified 451 serum proteins. Machine learning models defined a four-marker panel (HABP2, CD163, AFP, PIVKA-II) that distinguished HCC from cirrhosis (LC) patients in an independent validation cohort (AUC 0.979, sensitivity 0.925, specificity 0.915), reported as outperforming existing clinical prediction strategies. The machine learning role is panel modelling within a proteomics pipeline; this is a 2023 preprint read from its abstract only.
ai_technology: Machine learning models combining serum proteins and clinical markers into a diagnostic panel
organization: Fujian Medical University; Mengchao Hepatobiliary Hospital

evidence.tested: Serum proteomic markers and a machine-learning panel for HCC versus cirrhosis in discovery and independent validation cohorts of 662 individuals.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical benefit and whether the panel works outside the studied cohorts; preprint not peer reviewed; full text not reviewed.
